citations.title: City snapshot: Kris Licht to become Reckitt Benckiser CEO next month

sentences.text: Kris Licht was appointed CEO Designate of Reckitt Benckiser Group on 1 May 2023, became an Executive Director on 1 June 2023 and took over as Chief Executive Officer on 1 October 2023, succeeding Nicandro Durante.

sentences.quote: Licht had served as president of Reckitt's health business and as chief customer officer since July 2020. Prior to this, he served as Reckitt's chief transformation officer from November 2019 to July 2020.
sentences.text: He joined the company as Chief Transformation Officer in November 2019 and from July 2020 served as President of Reckitt's Health business and Chief Customer Officer, a period in which Reckitt said its health global business unit grew revenues by 1.4 billion pounds over three years.

sentences.quote: He joined Reckitt from PepsiCo, where he held a variety of senior operational and strategic leadership positions. Prior to PepsiCo, he was a Partner at McKinsey & Co with a focus on the consumer, health and retail practices.
sentences.text: Before Reckitt he held senior operational and strategic leadership roles at PepsiCo, and prior to that was a partner at McKinsey & Company focused on consumer, health and retail.

mgmt_bio.text: He joined the company as Chief Transformation Officer in November 2019 and from July 2020 served as President of Reckitt's Health business and Chief Customer Officer, a period in which Reckitt said its health global business unit grew revenues by 1.4 billion pounds over three years. Before Reckitt he held senior operational and strategic leadership roles at PepsiCo, and prior to that was a partner at McKinsey & Company focused on consumer, health and retail.

sentences.text: Kris Licht remains chief executive, with Shannon Eisenhardt as chief financial officer.

sentences.quote: Reckitt Benckiser Group plc (the "Company" or "Reckitt") today announces the appointment of Harry Kirsch, current CFO of Novartis Pharma AG and Deepak Nath, current CEO of Smith+Nephew plc, to the Board as Non-Executive Directors, effective 1 April 2026.
sentences.text: Harry Kirsch, CFO of Novartis Pharma, and Deepak Nath, CEO of Smith+Nephew, joined the board as non-executive directors on 1 April 2026, as Margherita Della Valle and Mahesh Madhavan retired; Deborah Waterhouse and Gavin Patterson were appointed non-executive directors from 1 July 2026, joining the audit and remuneration committees respectively.

sentences.quote: Our Fuel for Growth programme is reducing fixed costs, driving efficiency and providing us with greater capacity to invest.
sentences.text: At the 2026 half-year results Licht said growth accelerated in the second quarter and that the Fuel for Growth programme is reducing fixed costs and creating capacity to invest, while reiterating medium-term guidance of 4-5% like-for-like net revenue growth for Core Reckitt.

mgmt_recent.text: Harry Kirsch, CFO of Novartis Pharma, and Deepak Nath, CEO of Smith+Nephew, joined the board as non-executive directors on 1 April 2026, as Margherita Della Valle and Mahesh Madhavan retired; Deborah Waterhouse and Gavin Patterson were appointed non-executive directors from 1 July 2026, joining the audit and remuneration committees respectively. At the 2026 half-year results Licht said growth accelerated in the second quarter and that the Fuel for Growth programme is reducing fixed costs and creating capacity to invest, while reiterating medium-term guidance of 4-5% like-for-like net revenue growth for Core Reckitt. He has also kept Mead Johnson classified as non-core while reviewing options for it.

citations.quote: This was supported by the Fuel for Growth cost reduction programme, which trimmed fixed costs by 150 basis points to 19.4% of net revenue.
citations.title: Reckitt beats its own targets and signals confidence in 2026 after year of strategic progress

sentences.quote: the Fuel for Growth cost reduction programme, which trimmed fixed costs by 150 basis points to 19.4% of net revenue
sentences.text: Public reporting indicates that under Kris Licht, Reckitt has delivered on its announced strategy: the Essential Home divestment to Advent International completed on 31 December 2025, with Reckitt retaining a 30% equity stake, and the Fuel for Growth programme trimmed fixed costs by 150 basis points to 19.4% of net revenue.

Capital returns have been substantial, with GBP 6.4 billion returned since July 2024, a 5% higher interim dividend and a new buyback of up to GBP 500 million, plus roughly USD 2.2 billion via special dividend and share consolidation.
